grh_49ddc4f489da8bed2ac4.title: The Vagabond Veteran
paragraphs: Larry, a discharged fighter pilot, collapses in a Rivers End cafe convinced that recurring panic, suffocation and depression mean he is going insane. Dr. Christian recognizes a severe combat-nerves reaction rather than physical disease and brings Larry home instead of returning him to a hospital. Larry has no real home to return to, and the pressure and noise of a factory job after discharge only made his symptoms worse. Christian places him with the warm Santos family, where quiet routine and friendship with young Ted begin to restore him. A sudden startle in the garden makes Larry swing at Christian, terrifying him that he really is dangerous, but Christian refuses to give up on him. Later, while fishing with Christian and Ted, Christian falls into deep water. Larry reacts instantly, dives in and pulls him to safety without freezing or losing control. The emergency proves more convincingly than any reassurance that Larry's mind still functions under pressure. He accepts that he is recovering and agrees to stay with the Santos family, gaining the stable home and human connection he had been missing since the war.

grh_495b7f70d6b0fe8aa7c9.title: The Perfect Hostess
paragraphs: Wealthy Samson Cuthbert, trapped in a failing marriage to society-perfect Margery, secretly discusses having her killed while he is away on a western business trip. The hired killer's attempt fails, and family friend Dr. Woolsey uncovers enough of the scheme to test Samson with a false telegram announcing Margery's death. When Samson returns and finds his wife alive and sincerely offering to rebuild their marriage, he interprets her presence as torment and kills her himself. At the evening dinner party he continues speaking to Margery although none of the guests can see her, leading Woolsey to realize what has happened and send for the police.

grh_495b37ff8b1a7f305008.title: Operation In A Shack
paragraphs: Dr. Christian leaves Rivers End for a fishing vacation with Swampy and reaches a remote river shack to find young Jimmy unconscious with a ruptured appendix. The nearest hospital is about seventy miles away and Jimmy cannot survive the trip, while the doctor has neither surgical instruments nor proper facilities. Faced with almost certain death if he does nothing, Dr. Christian improvises an operating room in the shack, boiling water and using the knives and materials available to perform the emergency operation. Jimmy survives, and news of the feat brings Dr. Christian unexpected professional attention and the possibility of greater opportunities in the city. He ultimately remains in Rivers End, reminded that the ordinary patients who depend on their country doctor are the work he chose.
